public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# The Lovász–Plummer conjecture (proved 2011) and Sheehan's conjecture

*References:*
* [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Petersen%27s_theorem#Related_conjectures)
* [LP86] Lovász, L. and Plummer, M. D. (1986). *Matching Theory.* North-Holland.
* [EKKKN11] Esperet, L., Kardoš, F., King, A. D., Král', D. and Norine, S. (2011).
  "Exponentially many perfect matchings in cubic graphs." *Adv. Math.* 227, pp. 1646--1664.
  [arXiv:1012.2878](https://arxiv.org/abs/1012.2878)
* [Sh77] Sheehan, J. (1977). "The multiplicity of Hamiltonian circuits in a graph." In *Recent
  Advances in Graph Theory*, Academia, Prague, pp. 477--480.
* [Th98] Thomassen, C. (1998). "Independent dominating sets and a second Hamiltonian cycle in
  regular graphs." *J. Combin. Theory Ser. B* 72, pp. 104--109.
-/

@[expose] public section

open SimpleGraph

namespace LovaszPlummerConjecture

variable {V : Type*}

/-- The number of perfect matchings of `G`. -/
noncomputable def perfectMatchingCount (G : SimpleGraph V) : ℕ :=
  {M : G.Subgraph | M.IsPerfectMatching}.ncard

/--
**The Lovász–Plummer conjecture (1970s), proved by Esperet, Kardoš, King, Král' and Norine
(2011).**

Every bridgeless cubic graph on $n$ vertices has exponentially many perfect matchings: there is
a constant $c > 0$ such that the number of perfect matchings is at least $2^{cn}$.
[EKKKN11] prove this with $2^{n/3656}$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem lovasz_plummer_conjecture :
    ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]
      (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj],
      (∀ v, G.degree v = 3) → G.IsBridgeless →
      (2 : ℝ) ^ (c * Fintype.card V) ≤ perfectMatchingCount G := by
  sorry

/--
**The explicit bound of Esperet–Kardoš–King–Král'–Norine (2011).**

Every bridgeless cubic graph on $n$ vertices has at least $2^{n/3656}$ perfect matchings.

*Reference:* [EKKKN11].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem lovasz_plummer_conjecture.variants.explicit
    {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    (hcubic : ∀ v, G.degree v = 3) (hbridgeless : G.IsBridgeless) :
    (2 : ℝ) ^ ((Fintype.card V : ℝ) / 3656) ≤ perfectMatchingCount G := by
  sorry

/-- A **Hamiltonian cycle** of `G`: a cycle passing through every vertex. -/
def IsHamiltonianCycle (G : SimpleGraph V) {v : V} (c : G.Walk v v) : Prop :=
  c.IsCycle ∧ ∀ w, w ∈ c.support

/--
**Sheehan's conjecture (1977).**

Every $4$-regular graph with a Hamiltonian cycle has a second Hamiltonian cycle (one with a
different edge set). Sheehan's conjecture would settle the last open case of the question,
raised by Smith's theorem for cubic graphs, of which regular Hamiltonian graphs have a second
Hamiltonian cycle: Thomassen [Th98] proved it for all $r$-regular graphs with $r \ge 300$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem sheehan_conjecture :
    ∀ {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj],
      (∀ v, G.degree v = 4) →
      ∀ (v : V) (c : G.Walk v v), IsHamiltonianCycle G c →
        ∃ (w : V) (c' : G.Walk w w), IsHamiltonianCycle G c' ∧
          c'.edges.toFinset ≠ c.edges.toFinset := by
  sorry

/--
**Thomassen (1998): regular graphs of large degree.**

Every $r$-regular Hamiltonian graph with $r \ge 300$ has a second Hamiltonian cycle.

*Reference:* [Th98].
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5]
theorem sheehan_conjecture.variants.thomassen
    {V : Type} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (G : SimpleGraph V) [DecidableRel G.Adj]
    (r : ℕ) (hr : 300 ≤ r) (hreg : ∀ v, G.degree v = r)
    (v : V) (c : G.Walk v v) (hc : IsHamiltonianCycle G c) :
    ∃ (w : V) (c' : G.Walk w w), IsHamiltonianCycle G c' ∧
      c'.edges.toFinset ≠ c.edges.toFinset := by
  sorry

end LovaszPlummerConjecture

findings.description: The theorem heading dates Sheehan's conjecture to 1977, and the module bibliography likewise dates “The multiplicity of Hamiltonian circuits in a graph” to 1977 under [Sh77]. That proceedings contribution was published in 1975. This is a bibliographic slip only; the Lean statement correctly expresses the conjecture.
findings.source_evidence: Goedgebeur–Meersman–Zamfirescu, “Graphs with few Hamiltonian Cycles,” arXiv:1812.05650, bibliography, lists this contribution in Recent Advances in Graph Theory, pp. 477–480 (1975), separately from Sheehan's different 1977 paper “Graphs with exactly one hamiltonian circuit.” Its Sheehan subsection dates the proposal to 1974. Brinkmann–De Pauw, arXiv:2304.08946, bibliography, independently gives the proceedings publication year as 1975.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the bibliography entry to [Sh75], Sheehan (1975). Remove 1977 from the theorem heading, or distinguish the 1974 proposal from its 1975 publication. No mathematical statement needs changing.

reformulations.difference: The displayed Lovász–Plummer conjecture in EKKKN includes the upper bound |M(G)| ≤ 2^|V(G)| as well as the exponential lower bound; Lean states only the lower bound.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The upper bound is automatic for cubic graphs. Recursively choosing the matching edge at the first unmatched vertex gives at most three choices per matched pair, hence at most 3^(n/2) ≤ 2^n perfect matchings. Odd-order graphs have none, and the empty graph has one. Thus adding the source's upper bound imposes no additional condition.

reformulations.difference: EKKKN's main theorem allows loopless multigraphs, whereas the Lean theorem quantifies over simple graphs.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The same bound for simple graphs implies the multigraph version without changing 3656. Replace each pair of vertices joined by exactly two parallel edges by a diamond K₄ minus an edge, attaching the two external edges at its degree-two vertices. Both two-terminal pieces have 2, 0, 0, 1 matching completions when neither, just the first, just the second, or both terminals are matched externally. Replace each triple-edge component by K₄; both have three perfect matchings. These replacements preserve bridgeless cubicity and the total matching count, eliminate parallel edges, and increase the vertex count. Applying the simple-graph bound therefore implies the original multigraph bound. The reverse implication is immediate. The local matching profiles were checked computationally in Lean, but the complete reduction was not formalized.

reformulations.difference: The literature states that no uniquely Hamiltonian 4-regular graph exists. Lean instead requires a second Hamiltonian cycle with a different edge set for every supplied Hamiltonian-cycle walk.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For a fixed graph, form the set of edge finsets realized by Hamiltonian cycles. The Lean condition holds exactly when this set does not have a unique element: it is vacuous when there are no Hamiltonian cycles, and otherwise every realized edge set must have a different realized edge set. This graphwise equivalence was proved in the scratch file. The custom Hamiltonian-cycle predicate was also proved equivalent to Mathlib's definition; reversal and re-rooting preserve the compared edge finset.

sources_consulted: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Petersen%27s_theorem — particularly “Number of perfect matchings in cubic bridgeless graphs”; the cited Related_conjectures anchor is no longer present.

Esperet–Kardoš–King–Král'–Norine, arXiv:1012.2878v2: https://arxiv.org/abs/1012.2878 and https://arxiv.org/e-print/1012.2878 — introduction, main theorem, graph conventions, concluding remarks and bibliography.
Goedgebeur–Meersman–Zamfirescu, “Graphs with few Hamiltonian Cycles,” arXiv:1812.05650, 2019 version: https://arxiv.org/e-print/1812.05650 — introduction, Sheehan subsection and bibliography.

Brinkmann–De Pauw, “Uniquely hamiltonian graphs for many sets of degrees,” arXiv:2304.08946, 2024 version: https://arxiv.org/e-print/2304.08946 — introduction, graph conventions, concluding remarks and bibliography.
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamiltonian_path — definitions of Hamiltonian paths and cycles.

review.notes: No substantive mathematical misformalization or status discrepancy found. All six declarations were checked. Lean experiments in /workspace/review/scratch.lean compile successfully: the matching collection is finite on theorem inputs; matching subgraphs are determined by their edge sets; the empty graph has exactly one perfect matching; degree hypotheses exclude problematic small nonempty graphs; and K₅ has two explicitly verified Hamiltonian cycles with different edge sets. The original full texts of LP86, Sheehan's proceedings contribution, and Th98 were not obtained. Their relevant claims are explicitly reproduced in the accessible research papers listed above; the Thomassen bound was checked through Goedgebeur–Meersman–Zamfirescu's account. No repository files were edited.
